Evaluation criteria: "Business Success" Judges evaluate to what degree they trust that an investor could be interested in investing in such an IT product, to the same degree as whether the owners of such an IT product will be able to earn a lot of money. "World Impact" If this product becomes popular and is used by every person on Earth, to what degree will it somehow change the life of humanity. "Most Viable Product" After the Hackathon, you have 2 months during which you launch your IT product and, at the end of the 2 months, submit your video with statistics showing that people are using your product. It doesn't matter, paid or free. Those who will be claiming the prize places may have a call with the Organizers so that the Organizers can validate the provided data. Can you run ads? = Yes. Can you advertise for free? = Yes. Are paying users needed, or will free users be counted? = The data presented by the Participants (Hackers) will be analyzed, and scores will be assigned according to the current competition of the projects' success. "A Real Product from Start to Business" Participants' projects will be evaluated 1 year after the end of the Hackathon. The same rules as in "Most Viable Product." Criteria for evaluation by Judges of "Business Success," "World Impact": Positive factors: MVP works = the declared functions work without errors. Negative factors: A function is declared as working, but doesn't work. The interface is complicated to interact with. Rules for creating the IT product: Judges test immediately Logging in Registration Payment functions Judges test immediately = no logging in / registration / payment. Focus your attention on the functions that you offer to potential Clients, skip logging in / registration, payment. Criteria for evaluation by Judges relating only to "World Impact": a limited number of countries and/or a target audience better EVERY person Negative factors: The product is applicable to a limited number of countries and/or a target audience = better that the user could be EVERY person. Criteria for evaluation by Judges of the Video Presentation: Positive factors: The Video Presentation shows the "successful Client path" = the Participant shows what the Judge must press in order to test the functionality that the Team/Participant is demonstrating. Negative factors: The video tells plans, a market overview, and similar reasoning about the future, instead of performing the task = show where the User must "poke" in order to get a RESULT from the IT product. Criteria for evaluation by Judges of the Questionnaire: ≤ 300 characters per answer 300 Positive factors: Answers to the questions are given briefly and to the point of the questions asked. Aim for no more than 300 characters of answer for each item. Negative factors: Text of more than 300 characters of answer for each item. Answers are not relevant to the questions asked. Common mistakes: many functions 1 function that really works Trying to create many functions = create 1 function, but one that will actually work well, not a prototype. To achieve the above-named goals, Judges, according to their inner convictions, may take into account: Whether this IT product can be successful and/or useful to users/the world. The intuitive clarity of the interface. The declared functionality and the actual one: a simulated DB or a real backend, real data or a stub/example, if there is a button, whether it works (if there is no functionality behind the button, don't declare it in your product). The presence of test coverage for the product's resilience to changes: basic smoke testing. A clear business model of monetization (applicable to "Business Success," may be ignored for the "World Impact" track). The correct product vision. Creating the correct application architecture, with the aim of its scaling and commercialization.
